title: David Ellison has built a Hollywood giant in Skydance. Now he wants to make it a tech company
key_facts: The merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery took effect on Tuesday (6 Oct 2026); the combined company is called Skydance.
CEO David Ellison, 43, and co-CEO Ynon Kreiz say technology and AI tools will be used throughout the business and the streaming tech stacks will be unified.
The combined company will have more than 200 million streaming subscribers and roughly $80 billion in debt.
Skydance says most cost savings will come from 'technology, integration and procurement, marketing and real estate rationalization'.
Analyst Ross Benes of eMarketer told CNN that when executives promise to tech-ify the company, 'I hear layoffs'.
Opponents, including NYU professor Janet Grillo, say consolidation limits opportunities for storytellers.
CNN says it became part of Skydance as of Tuesday.
quote_evidence: Skydance said Tuesday that most of the cost savings will come from “technology, integration and procurement, marketing and real estate rationalization.”
When Skydance executives promise to tech-ify the company, “I hear layoffs,” eMarketer Senior Analyst Ross Benes told CNN.
why_it_matters_hint: The merged company says AI and tech are central to its plan, while it carries heavy debt and must cut costs.
notes: CNN discloses it is now owned by Skydance.
